    --exclude <id>    keep one database or cache (repeatable)

Usage: velixir fork [--at <moment>] [options]
         velixir fork list | status <fork-id> | discard <fork-id>

  A separate copy of the app as it was at a moment (default: now), with its own copies of
  the data. Use it to reproduce a bug against real data, or to hand an agent a safe copy
  of production. It bills like any app while it runs; discard it when you're done.

  The copy can't reach the internet unless you pass --unsealed: it has this app's env vars,
  live API keys included.

  Options take the same --at and --no-* / --exclude flags as 'velixir rewind', plus:

         velixir rewind apply|undo <rewind-id> [--yes]
         velixir rewind list | status <rewind-id>

  Take the app back to a moment. 'rewind' builds a preview on its own URL with its own

  databases and caches are never overwritten, so an applied rewind can be undone.

  Moments:
    --at "30m ago" | "2h ago" | "1d ago" | now
    --at "2026-10-16 09:41"        your local time
    --at "2026-10-16T08:41:00Z"    UTC (or any offset)

  Leave parts out (they stay as they are now):
    --no-code         keep today's release
    --no-config       keep today's env vars and settings
    --no-databases    keep the databases as they are
    --no-caches       keep the caches as they are
    --no-files        keep the volume as it is
    --exclude <id>    keep one database or cache (repeatable)

  Options:
    --app, -a <id>    App ID (default: the linked project)
    --no-wait         Start and return; check with 'velixir rewind status <id>'
    --yes, -y         Apply or undo without the confirmation prompt
    --json            Raw JSON

  Examples:
    velixir rewind plan --at "2h ago"
    velixir rewind --at "2h ago" --no-databases      code, config, caches and files only
    velixir rewind apply 3f2504e0-4f89-11d3-9a0c-0305e82c3301

Usage: velixir fork [--at <moment>] [options]
         velixir fork list | status <fork-id> | discard <fork-id>

  A separate copy of the app as it was at a moment (default: now), with its own copies of
  the data. Use it to reproduce a bug against real data, or to hand an agent a safe copy
  of production. It bills like any app while it runs; discard it when you're done.

  The copy can't reach the internet unless you pass --unsealed: it has this app's env vars,
  live API keys included.

  Options take the same --at and --no-* / --exclude flags as 'velixir rewind', plus:
    --unsealed        Let the copy reach the internet (its background jobs act for real)
    --no-wait         Start and return
    --app, -a <id>    App ID (default: the linked project)
    --json            Raw JSON

Usage: velixir replay <release> [options]
         velixir replay status <replay-id> | list

  Test a built release against your real recent traffic before it goes live. Two sealed
  copies of the app are made from the same moment, one on the live release and one on
  <release>, and recent GET requests go to both. You get new errors, status changes,
  changed responses and slower routes; values that change on every request are ignored.

  <release> is a release ID or its version, like v12.

  Options:
    --window, -w <t>  How far back to read traffic: 1h to 7d (default 24h)
    --max, -n <n>     Distinct requests to replay, 10 to 1000 (default 300)
    --keep-copies     Leave both copies running afterwards
    --wait            Block until the verdict. Exit code 1 on regressions, for CI
    --app, -a <id>    App ID (default: the linked project)
    --json            Raw JSON

  Example (CI): deploy the new build to a staging slot, then
    velixir replay v42 --wait     fails the job on regressions, so promote only after it
